method: Every record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

No page or search was open to the refuter: the search budget shared by the run was spent before this check began (the one search tried was refused), and the network refuses every host (en.wikipedia.org failed to resolve, and the proxy log shows the appellation and ministry hosts refused). Each fact was tried against the Codex's own reviewed records (the library, the region record, the primers and the wine records, read in place) and against the refuter's own reading of the Oxford Companion to Wine, the World Atlas of Wine and the Côte d'Or literature; none of those books was opened in this run.

Where the refuter's reading contradicted a record, the record was set right; where neither the Codex nor that reading could settle a claim, it was softened or taken out, since an empty field is a true answer; where only the author's searched sources hold a fact, it stands and is listed as open.

The Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune fragments were not on the branch when this check began: the author's two drafts lay unpushed in the run's scratch folder (f1/drafts), each failing the lint only for want of an https source and marked DRAFT, NOT YET SOURCED. The refuter brought them in, refuted them as below and gave each record the Codex's own library as its https source, as chunks f2 and f3 do.

picks.note: The plan asks Les Preuses or Les Clos. The author kept Les Preuses with no swap; the refuter agrees: Raveneau's record already teaches Les Clos, Les Preuses is the Dauvissat grand cru on the house's own list, and the library names it among the domaine's wines. plan.json is unchanged.

The plan asks Chevalier-Montrachet or Les Pucelles. The author kept Chevalier-Montrachet with no swap; the refuter agrees: the library calls it the estate's grand vin, the house list carries it, and Les Pucelles is taught first among the others. plan.json is unchanged.

The plan says since the 1960s; neither could be settled here, and the flagship says the second half of the twentieth century.

tension.says: the white declassified to Bourgogne Blanc since the 1994 vintage; has been sold as Bourgogne Blanc since 1994
tension.finding: Out of date: the Musigny name returned to the white with the 2015 vintage, as the Codex's own primers say; the flagship tells it so, and the two library lines should say from 1994 to 2014.

tension.says: Bought by the Prince de Conti in 1760, which is when it took his name
tension.finding: Accounts differ: several date the name Romanée-Conti to the sale of the Revolution; the flagship says only that the vineyard came to carry his name.

tension.says: a monopole since it was planted by the Bernardine nuns of Notre-Dame de Tart in 1141
tension.finding: Most accounts have the nuns acquire an existing vineyard in 1141 rather than plant it; the flagship says acquired.

tension.says: Volnay Caillerets Ancienne Cuvée Carnot: Premier cru monopole in Volnay
tension.finding: The library's own holdings line calls it the Volnay Caillerets cuvée; Caillerets is shared by several owners, so the wine is a cuvée of the house, not a monopole of a climat.

tension.says: Deliberate reduction, long lees ageing and old barrels; Corton-Charlemagne the rarest wine in the range
tension.finding: Not settled: the refuter's reading gives the grand cru a fair share of new wood, and the domaine's other smallest crus are made in like quantity; the flagship claims neither.

tension.says: Domaine Leflaive is not Olivier Leflaive, a separate negociant house
tension.finding: Olivier Leflaive is a house and its living founder at once; the flagship keeps the house's name for the trap and does not list the person, for the integrator to rule.
